<action type="say">
Here’s exactly what to do next.

1) Block the card and request a replacement  
Use ONE of these right away (whichever you can access fastest):

• Mobile app / website  
  - Go to: Cards (or Accounts → Credit Card)  
  - Select your credit card  
  - Choose: “Report card lost or stolen” → pick “Lost”  
  - Confirm you want it blocked immediately  
  - When asked about a new card, select: “Yes, send me a replacement” and confirm your existing mailing address  

• Phone (if you can’t get into the app/website)  
  - Call the customer service/emergency card number on our website  
  - Say: “My only credit card with you is lost. Please block it immediately and send a replacement to the address on file.”  
  - Stay on the line until they confirm the card is blocked and a new one has been ordered.

2) What happens to charges and payments  
Once it’s blocked:  
- New charges with the lost card number should be declined.  
- Your replacement card will have a new number, expiry, and CVV, but the same account.  
- Any merchant that already has an approved transaction (e.g., something you bought earlier today) may still post, but future attempts should fail.

3) Handling your subscriptions (Netflix, phone bill, etc.)  
After you get the new card details:

A simple way to build a list of what to update:  
- Log in to your online banking/app  
- Go to your credit card → “Transactions” or “Activity”  
- Filter or scroll back a few months and note any repeated monthly charges (same merchant around the same day each month). Typical ones:
  - Streaming (Netflix, Spotify, etc.)  
  - Phone/internet provider  
  - Cloud storage (iCloud, Google, etc.)  
  - Gyms, subscription boxes, software services  

Then, for each subscription:  
- Sign in to that service’s website/app  
- Go to Billing/Payment/Subscriptions  
- Update the card number, expiry, and CVV with your new card details.

4) Extra safety steps  
- Once you know the card is blocked, don’t store the old number anywhere.  
- For the next 1–2 weeks, check your transactions list daily.  
  - If you see any charge you don’t recognize, contact us right away and say it’s unauthorized.  

If you tell me which bank/app you’re using (or what your online banking menu roughly looks like), I can give button-by-button instructions for reporting the card and, later, a checklist format you can use to track which subscriptions you’ve updated.</action>
